range.full_text:
A lawful Oath is a part of religious worship, wherein the person swearing in Truth, Righteousness, and Judgement, solemnly calleth God to witness what he sweareth; and to judge him according to the Truth or falseness thereof.

The Name of God only is that by which men ought to swear; and therein it is to be used, with all Holy Fear and reverence, therefore to swear vainly or rashly by that glorious, and dreadful name; or to swear at all by any other thing, is sinful and to be abhorred; yet as in matter of weight and moment for confirmation of truth, and ending all strife, an Oath is warranted by the Word of God; so a lawful Oath being imposed, by lawful Authority, in such matters, ought to be taken.

Whosoever taketh an Oath warranted by the Word of God, ought duely to consider the weightiness of so solemn an act; and therein to avouch nothing, but what he knoweth to be the truth; for that by rash, false, and vain Oaths the Lord is provoked, and for them this Land mournes.

An Oath is to be taken in the plain, and common sense of the words; without equivocation, or mental reservation.

A Vow which is not to be made to any Creature, but to God alone, is to be made and performed with all Religious care, and faithfulness: But Popish Monastical Vows, of perpetual single life, professed poverty, and regular obedience, are so far from being degrees of higher perfection, that they are superstitious, and sinful snares, in which no Christian may intangle himself.

proposed_edit.to: The Lord Jesus Christ hath taught us that we ought not to take oaths at all. We ought not to swear oaths upon things which are beyond our power and authority; and since we have no power and authority even to make one hair of our head black or white, we ought not to swear oaths at all.

annotations.note: Lord Jesus Christ told us to not take an oath at all: ““Again you have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall perform to the Lord what you have sworn.’ But I say to you, Do not take an oath at all, either by heaven, for it is the throne of God, or by the earth, for it is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. And do not take an oath by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black. Let what you say be simply ‘Yes’ or ‘No’; anything more than this comes from evil.” (Matthew 5:33-37)

annotations.note:
The Lord Jesus Christ told us: “Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place. For all who take the sword will perish by the sword.”” (Matthew 26:52)

The Lord Jesus Christ also taught us: “But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.” (Matthew 5:39) Christ Himself did no violence (Isaiah 53:9), and we are commanded to imitate the apostle Paul, as he imitates Christ (1 Corinthians 11:1). However, the Lord Jesus Christ escaped when He was brought to the brow of the hill to be thrown down (Luke 4:29). Therefore, Christians are allowed to escape danger. The sentence on Christians holding the office of magistrate is removed, so that the Confession is silent on that question.

As it is of the Law of nature, that in general a proportion of time by Gods appointment, be set a part for the Worship of God; so by his Word in a positive-moral, and perpetual Commandement, binding all men, in all Ages, he hath particularly appointed one day in seven for a Sabbath to be kept holy unto him, which from the beginning of the World to the Resurrection of Christ, was the last day of the week; and from the resurrection of Christ, was changed into the first day of the week which is called the Lords day; and is to be continued to the end of the World, as the Christian Sabbath; the observation of the last day of the week being abolished.

The Sabbath is then kept holy unto the Lord, when men after a due preparing of their hearts, and ordering their common affairs aforehand, do not only observe an holy rest all the day, from their own works, words, and thoughts, about their worldly employment, and recreations, but also are taken up the whole time in the publick and private exercises of his worship, and in the duties of necessity and mercy.

proposed_edit.from:
As it is of the Law of nature, that in general a proportion of time by Gods appointment, be set a part for the Worship of God; so by his Word in a positive-moral, and perpetual Commandement, binding all men, in all Ages, he hath particularly appointed one day in seven for a Sabbath to be kept holy unto him, which from the beginning of the World to the Resurrection of Christ, was the last day of the week; and from the resurrection of Christ, was changed into the first day of the week which is called the Lords day; and is to be continued to the end of the World, as the Christian Sabbath; the observation of the last day of the week being abolished.

The Sabbath is then kept holy unto the Lord, when men after a due preparing of their hearts, and ordering their common affairs aforehand, do not only observe an holy rest all the day, from their own works, words, and thoughts, about their worldly employment, and recreations, but also are taken up the whole time in the publick and private exercises of his worship, and in the duties of necessity and mercy.

annotations.note: Christ is our Sabbath: “Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” (Matthew 11:28) Also, see Hebrew 4:3. The command to keep the Sabbath in the law pointed to Him: “Therefore let no one pass judgment on you in questions of food and drink, or with regard to a festival or a new moon or a Sabbath.” (Colossians 2:16)

proposed_edit.to: and they are his servants for the good of Justice, to shew his wrath against evil doers; yet the violence which they commit is evil in it self, and God, who turneth to good what men mean for evil, doth use it to the ends of his Justice.

annotations.note: Government is God's servant for the good of justice being shown against evil (Romans 13:4), but its own violence is evil; whatever they mean for evil, God uses for good (Genesis 50:20). God providentially uses governments, just like Assyria (Isaiah 10:5), Babylon (Jeremiah 25:9) and King Cyrus (Isaiah 45:1). God uses the evil of violence committed by governments for His good purposes of justice. However, this does not cancel out the church's responsibility to preach against all evil, including the evil of violence committed by governments.

proposed_edit.to:
**3.** It is the duty of the Churches to preach all that Christ hath commanded, to all Nations, and to their Governments also, and to testify against all evil, even the evil of violence committed by Governments. For the Sword which Christ hath given to his Church is the Sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God that judgeth our thoughts and intentions. The Lord Jesus Christ ruleth by judging by the Sword of the Spirit; and we rule with him as Kings, and to us he hath given authority to judge by the Sword of the Spirit. By this Sword God doth, in the preaching of the Gospel, restrain and judge evil; and this is a more excellent way of shewing Justice, because God can at the same time shew mercy to the sinner; and all who are saved do themselves preach the Gospel, instead of dying also. And it is the will of God that by the preaching of the Gospel Nations shall beat their swords into plowshares, and learn war no more; which, though the Beast hath authority over every Nation throughout this present age, is in part fulfilled therein, and shall be fully accomplished in the new heaven and the new earth.

**4.** Civil Magistrates being set up

annotations.note: We are supposed to preach all that the Lord Jesus Christ commanded us (including the command not to take the sword) to all nations (including governments) (Matthew 28:20). It is the will of God that, as a result of the preaching of the Gospel, the nations will beat their swords into plowshares and no longer learn war during the Messianic or church age (Isaiah 2:4). (We know that Isaiah 2:1-4 describes the Messianic age because of the parallels between Isaiah 2:4 and Isaiah 11:4-6, which describes the Messianic age.) At the same time, the book of Revelation teaches that the beast was given authority over every nation throughout the church age (Revelation 13:7). As a result, the vision from Isaiah 2, in which all nations will become peaceful, will be fully realized only in the new heaven and the new earth (Revelation 21:24-25). However, it is, and will be, partially realized in the church age. In the New Testament God uses the sword of the Spirit (the preaching of the Gospel; Ephesians 6:17; Hebrews 4:12; cf. 2 Corinthians 10:4) to restrain and judge evil. It is a more excellent way of showing justice because God can at the same time show mercy to the sinner. All who are saved themselves preach the Gospel instead of dying also. Also, the Lord Jesus Christ rules by judging by the sword of the Spirit (the word of God that judges our thoughts and intentions). We rule with him as kings and to us He gave authority to judge by the sword of the Spirit (Revelation 20:4). Revelation 19:15 makes the link between the Lord Jesus Christ ruling and judging by the sword of the Spirit: “From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and he will rule them with a rod of iron.” This edit inserts a new paragraph 24.3 and renumbers the old 24.3 as 24.4.
